value.rationale: The smallest closed histogram (three categories) gives a natural noise-variance calibration problem. Its fully dependent contrast structure has a strict uniform local maximum but a larger less-balanced boundary value; this exact local-global paradox proves that no monotone majorization or quasi-concavity shortcut applies to optimization/bounding. Explicit negative Hessian and boundary values provide a structural diagnostic beyond generic folded-normal covariance formulas. No global optimizer is asserted.
